bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502928 (freeradius-server): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer_dns [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502928
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable FreeRADIUS checkout `3bb7cd828f502473dc533572a4b3ef33694a9568`, the exact 13-byte witness `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff` gives `fr_dns_decode()` a 12-byte DNS header plus a 1-byte trailing question buffer. `decode_record()` uses header bytes `[4,5] == 0x20 0x20` as question count `0x2020`, so it attempts to decode the first question from that 1-byte tail. The question-name field reaches `decode_dns_labels()` with `data = packet + 12` and `data_len = 1`, but the vulnerable call computes the third argument to `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` as `data + data_len - packet_ctx->packet`, i.e. the packet-relative offset `13`, instead of the current field length `1`. `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` therefore sets `end = buf + 13`, believes 13 label bytes remain starting at the final packet byte, sees the lone byte `0xff` as a compressed-label pointer lead byte, and lets the truncated-pointer guard `if ((p + 2) > end)` pass. The next statement `offset = p[1];` then reads 1 byte 0 bytes past the 13-byte heap testcase allocation, matching the saved AddressSanitizer stack `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length -> decode_dns_labels -> decode_value_trampoline`. The patch matches this exact obligation by replacing the packet-relative expression with `data_len` in both the `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` and `fr_dns_labels_network_verify()` calls.

source.description: First project-side parse that materializes the post-header question sub-buffer and its explicit remaining length. For the exact witness, skipping the 12-byte DNS header leaves a 1-byte tail that becomes the current question data.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` bytes are exactly `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff`. With `packet_len == 13` and `DNS_HDR_LEN == 12`, this step makes `p = packet + 12` and `end - p = 1`, so only the final `0xff` byte remains for question decoding.

tainted_value_origin.code:
slen = fr_struct_from_network(ctx, cursor, attr, p, end - p, true,
			      packet_ctx, decode_value_trampoline, NULL);
tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the 1-byte post-header tail and the original packet context enter the question struct decoder together. On the crashing iteration, that state reaches `decode_dns_labels()` as `data = packet + 12`, `data_len = 1`, while `packet_ctx->packet` still points at the start of the full 13-byte packet.

root_cause.code: slen = fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length(packet_ctx->packet, data, data + data_len - packet_ctx->packet, &next, packet_ctx->lb);
root_cause.description: Wrong length domain. `decode_dns_labels()` converts the end pointer of the current field into a packet-relative offset and passes that number as `buf_len`; for the witnessed sub-buffer at `packet + 12` with `data_len == 1`, the helper sees `13` instead of `1`. The patch replaces this exact expression with `data_len`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the caller inflated `end`, the compressed-pointer parser reads the second byte of a truncated two-byte pointer even though only the lone final `0xff` byte is inside the 13-byte testcase buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/lib/util/dns.c:958:13` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 13-byte heap region `[0x6020000000f0,0x6020000000fd)`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 13-byte witness passes the only explicit top-level size gate (`13 >= 12`), so the decoder proceeds past the fixed DNS header and reaches question decoding.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so the chain is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source, `patch.diff`, the saved AddressSanitizer traces, `reproduction_report.json`, and the exact staged `poc` bytes. Those artifacts are sufficient here because both the bad length computation and the crashing `p[1]` read are visible in source.
Stage 02 did not execute a fixed build. `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` below is source-grounded from the patch text matching the bad call site, not from dynamic differential validation.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 13-byte witness is split into a 12-byte DNS header and a 1-byte question tail `0xff`; header bytes `0x20 0x20` become question count `0x2020`, so the decoder attempts the first question parse on that one-byte tail.
The scalar DNS-label decoder calls `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` with packet-relative offset `13` as `buf_len` instead of the actual current-field length `1`.

The helper trusts the forged end pointer, treats the lone byte `0xff` as a compressed-pointer lead byte, skips the truncated-pointer rejection, and overreads `p[1]`, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. For the exact 13-byte witness `20 ... 20 ff`, this step skips the 12-byte DNS header and materializes the trailing sub-buffer for question decoding. That leaves `p = packet + 12`, `end = packet + 13`, and therefore exactly one remaining byte, `0xff`.

fine_trace.code:
count = fr_net_to_uint16(counter);
for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
fine_trace.note: Question-count bytes `[4,5] == 0x20 0x20` decode to `count == 0x2020` (`8224`), so the first loop iteration executes and the 1-byte tail from step 1 is actually presented as question data.

fine_trace.code:
slen = fr_struct_from_network(ctx, cursor, attr, p, end - p, true,
			      packet_ctx, decode_value_trampoline, NULL);
fine_trace.note: On iteration 0, `decode_record()` forwards `p = packet + 12` with `end - p = 1` into the question struct decoder. The saved stack confirms this one-byte buffer then reaches `decode_value_trampoline` and `decode_dns_labels()` as the current DNS-name field.

fine_trace.code: slen = fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length(packet_ctx->packet, data, data + data_len - packet_ctx->packet, &next, packet_ctx->lb);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. On the crashing path `data = packet + 12`, `data_len = 1`, and `packet_ctx->packet = packet`, so the third argument evaluates to `13`, the packet-relative end offset of the current field, instead of the current field length `1`. The patch replaces this argument with `data_len`.

With the wrong `buf_len == 13`, `start = *next = packet + 12` still passes the in-buffer check because `buf + buf_len` is miscomputed as `packet + 25`. The helper then sets `end = packet + 25` and now believes 13 label bytes remain starting at the last real packet byte.

The only real byte in the current label buffer is `0xff`, so the helper takes the compressed-pointer path. Because step 5 forged `end = packet + 25`, the truncated-pointer guard `(p + 2) > end` is false even though the 13-byte testcase allocation ends immediately after `p`.
Sink. After step 6 failed to reject the one-byte-truncated pointer, `offset = p[1]` reads the byte at absolute offset 13, which is 0 bytes past the 13-byte heap testcase allocation reported by ASan.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of the 13-byte heap buffer that libFuzzer allocated for the staged testcase contents.

format.name: 13-byte DNS decoder witness
format.contract: The staged evidence proves the exact 13-byte witness `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff`: twelve `0x20` bytes followed by a lone `0xff`. Its length `13` makes `fr_dns_decode()` leave a 1-byte post-header question buffer; header bytes `[4,5] == 0x20 0x20` make `decode_record()` attempt at least one question decode; and the final byte being an unpaired compressed-label lead byte `0xff` is what makes `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` take the compressed-pointer path once `decode_dns_labels()` miscomputes `buf_len` as `13`. The staged artifacts do not prove a broader input class.
